nodes.label: Journey Consistency
nodes.rationale: Every role needs one logical connected journey: Assessment -> Skill Graph -> weak skills -> Skill Studio -> Arena missions -> proof/Vault -> interview prep -> Portfolio -> Recruiter view; disconnected modules and dead ends are product bugs.

nodes.label: State Propagation QA
nodes.rationale: Whenever user data changes, trace all dependent systems: Arena completion -> ELO -> Aura -> Skill Graph -> Vault -> Recruiter View -> Launchpad -> Portfolio -> Analytics -> Timeline. Missing downstream updates are blocking bugs.

nodes.label: Feature-Folder Structure (features/<path>/<page>/)
nodes.rationale: Every page owns exactly PageName.jsx + tabs.config.js + components/ + hooks/ + index.js; domain logic is path-isolated (features/student/, features/professional/, etc.) so student and organization logic never cross-import.

nodes.label: challenge_attempts Table Schema
nodes.rationale: Per-attempt lifecycle (in_progress/submitted/evaluated/failed) carrying code_snapshot, execution_result, test_results, feedback, grade, and elo_delta.

nodes.label: challenges Table Schema
nodes.rationale: Canonical challenge catalog row: type/domain/difficulty/elo_impact/sandbox_type plus company sponsorship, recruiter visibility, and college/tag restrictions.

nodes.label: ELO Computation Model (computeEloUpdate)
nodes.rationale: Modified Elo formula: expected-score curve vs challenge ELO, K-factor scaled down as user ELO rises (48/36/28/20), 15%-per-retry attempt penalty, up-to-10% time-efficiency bonus, a floor of +3 ELO on any pass (score>=70), and a cap of -30 loss per submission to prevent cliff drops.

nodes.label: Mission Desk Homepage Redesign
nodes.rationale: Reorders the homepage around 'reporting for duty': Readiness Strip -> Mission Hero/Queue -> Proof Shelf -> only then the Practice Library below the fold; target time-to-mission-start < 10s.

nodes.label: One ELO Economy
nodes.rationale: Global ELO = weighted blend of role ELOs (active role x1.0, others x0.3); validation never changes ELO, only SCORED submissions do — keeps validating psychologically safe as 'how you work', not 'how you're judged'.

nodes.label: Capabilio Frontend Architecture Restructuring Plan
nodes.rationale: The stack is React+Vite SPA, not Next.js (no App Router/SSR/file-based routing); recommends staying on Vite + React Router v6 rather than migrating to Next.js, though the feature-folder structure would map directly to App Router route groups later with zero business-logic rework.

nodes.label: Arena Production Architecture v2
nodes.rationale: Every component is decided as if shipping to 10,000 concurrent users across 200 Indian colleges, 50 hiring companies, and an open professional pool; Arena is positioned as Capabilio's 'evidence layer' beside Pulse (visibility), Nexus (network), and Launchpad (opportunities).

nodes.label: Common Challenge Categories
nodes.rationale: Unlimited practice, curated, no AI generation, never touches ELO (XP+streak+skill mastery only per the blueprint's ELO/XP split); every category maps 1:1 onto an existing REUSE-flagged workstation so no new UI work is required to launch them.

nodes.label: Validator Contracts (§3)
nodes.rationale: Every validator is a pure function (submission, config) -> {passed, score(0-100), detail}; none write ELO/XP directly, that is the downstream ELO/XP Engine's job. Types: test_case_judge, ground_truth_compare, published_result_compare, live_render_probe, http_assertion, command_output_match, formula_result_check, kpi_compare, rubric_review, numeric_tolerance, register_match.

nodes.label: Workstation Compositions (§2)
nodes.rationale: Canonical mapping of UI modules (Code Editor, SQL Editor, Notebook Cell, Excel Grid, Diagram Canvas...) to composed Workstations (Code, SQL, Notebook, React/Frontend, API, Terminal...), each bound to a validator type and an artifact type.

nodes.label: 18-Domain Routing Table (§6)
nodes.rationale: Every role maps to a primary workstation plus secondaries chosen by asking 'what does this person's screen look like at work,' making the two historic offenders (system design in markdown, analyst output hidden until submission) structurally impossible via a workspace-allowlist validated at authoring time.

nodes.label: W7 BI Dashboard Studio
nodes.rationale: Data -> Build -> Present three-tab loop mirroring the analyst's real day; publishing a query result as KPI/Trend/Breakdown is the explicit bridge from computation to presentation, and Validate Metrics visibly mutates the Present dashboard (red outline on failing cards) rather than hiding output until submission.

nodes.label: Four-Slot Action Contract (§7)
nodes.rationale: Primary Run / Validate / Preview Proof / Submit are fixed bottom-bar slots with per-workstation labels; 'Run Tests' exists only where it's the actual job (W14) or the universal judge harness (W1) — canvas/document workstations hide the Run slot rather than inventing a fake verb.

nodes.label: W18 System Design Workspace
nodes.rationale: An architecture canvas is the workspace, not a markdown editor; Check Completeness runs the rubric as executable rules (orphan-node detection, required layers per prompt class, capacity arithmetic tolerance) that annotate the canvas directly.

nodes.label: Universal Challenge Shell
nodes.rationale: Identical outer frame for all 18 domains: top bar, left prompt rail (Brief/Data/Hints/History), center workstation renderer slot, right context rail (Live Checklist/Proof Preview), and a persistent 4-slot action bar (Run/Validate/Preview/Submit).

nodes.label: 16 Workstation Families (W1-W18)
nodes.rationale: Code IDE, Frontend Sandbox, API Workstation, Fullstack Studio, SQL Lab, Notebook Lab, BI Dashboard Studio, Data Pipeline Studio, Infra Terminal, Cloud Architecture Lab, SRE Console, Security Console, SOC IR Console, QA Test Lab, Analysis Board, Mobile Studio, AI/LLM Studio, System Design Workspace — each a self-contained renderer module with its own execution model (client-wasm/client-sandbox/simulated/server).

nodes.label: Validation vs Submission Logic (§8)
nodes.rationale: Validation is formative (unlimited, free, deterministic-only, mutates the live workspace, never touches ELO); submission is summative (scarce, immutable, adds AI evaluation, applies ELO). The old product blurred these — Validate buttons that did nothing and output only materializing at submission.

nodes.label: Challenge Payload Schema (FROZEN v1.0)
nodes.rationale: Single source-of-truth JSON contract (challengeType, workstation, validator, rewardRules, portfolioDecision, ...); the hard gate is owned by a first-class pipeline step, the Challenge Payload Validator, sitting between Challenge Engine and Workstation Router — missing/invalid payload/validator/rewardRules is rejected there and logged as an analytics event, never reaching the Workstation Router or frontend.

nodes.label: Difficulty Variants Framework (§5)
nodes.rationale: Worked Easy/Medium/Hard/Expert progressions across SQL Joins, React Component Build, DevOps Pipeline Fix, and Vulnerability Fix; each Challenge Template declares which tiers it actually supports, not every template needs all four.

nodes.label: Skill Dependency Graphs (40 roles)
nodes.rationale: Prerequisite chains (A -> B, A -> {B,C}) for all 40 IT roles across Software Engineering, Data & Analytics, Cloud/Platform/DevOps, Security, QA/Testing, Mobile/Emerging, and Business/Data-Adjacent families.

nodes.label: 4-Phase Build Order (§20.1)
nodes.rationale: Phase 1 ships the spine on the three workstations that already have real engines (W7/W5/W6, sql.js+Pyodide) to prove the whole thesis on the analyst cluster first; Phase 2 engineering, Phase 3 ops/simulation kit (shared vmModel+scenarioPlayer), Phase 4 long tail.

nodes.label: Challenge JSON Authoring Schema (§19.4)
nodes.rationale: Versioned authoring format binding role, workstation, stack_variants, validation checks, and proof_recipe; authoring CI rejects workstation/role mismatches, checks whose locus isn't in the declared panels, and any challenge with zero deterministic checks.

nodes.label: Supabase Data Model (§19.5)
nodes.rationale: attempts and scores tables carry no UPDATE policy at all in RLS — frozen means frozen at the database layer, not just an app-level convention.

nodes.label: Career Family Extension Point (§14)
nodes.rationale: careerFamily is reserved and hardcoded to 'IT' for all current work so that a future family (ECE, Mechanical, Civil, MBA, Healthcare...) becomes a new branch under an existing root instead of a schema migration across every existing challenge payload, skill graph, and portfolio record.

nodes.label: Five Hardest Risks & Mitigations (§20.2)
nodes.rationale: Simulator credibility (fewer, deeper scenarios > many shallow), Pyodide weight on Indian bandwidth (service-worker cache + lite-validation path), AI-scoring trust (deterministic floor >=60% of rubric), content velocity (challenge JSON + seed factory make variants cheap), and cheating/proof integrity (seeded per-user datasets + server re-execution + env_hash replay).

nodes.label: WorkstationModule Contract (§19.2)
nodes.rationale: A TypeScript interface (init/restore/collectValidatables/applyValidation/buildProofDraft/freeze/renderFrozen) that every workstation module must implement to register at all — Contracts B and C are enforced by the type system, not by review discipline.

nodes.label: Experience Consistency QA
nodes.rationale: Validate the app as the student using it: would this student believe the platform was designed specifically for them? An Embedded student must never see a Frontend journey; generic Software-Engineer fallbacks are avoided unless explicitly labeled as deliberate.

nodes.label: Student AI Coach Correctness Validation
nodes.rationale: Validates POST /api/copilot/coach against live Supabase JWTs/real ELO history/real ANTHROPIC_API_KEY spend by diffing every number Capi states against the student's real dashboard — any mismatch is P0.

nodes.label: Cross-Role Validation
nodes.rationale: Repeats the correctness prompts across all 7 streams (Embedded, Analog Layout, Mechanical, Civil, MBA, Pharmacy, Data Analyst) watching specifically for non-IT streams silently getting IT-flavored advice, the platform's single most likely failure mode given its IT-first history.

nodes.label: Failure-Mode / Fallback Validation
nodes.rationale: Flips ENABLE_MCP_COACH off/on in the real environment to confirm CopilotWidget.jsx's Groq-fallback logic fires correctly end-to-end in a live browser session — the sandbox test only proved the backend half (503 in ~40ms).

nodes.label: Coach Invocation Logging Verification
nodes.rationale: The /coach route emits one structured coach_invocation JSON log line per call (no new DB table); once confirmed real, these lines alone derive AI success rate, MCP failure rate, tool usage, latency, and top questions without a dedicated analytics backend.

nodes.label: Operational Readiness Checklist
nodes.rationale: Load test at realistic cohort size (the stdio MCP bridge is a single spawned process per backend instance, so concurrent tool calls queue through one client), monitoring, backups, and verifying aiLimiter thresholds before opening to a full college.

nodes.label: Capabilio Product Quality Standard
nodes.rationale: Capabilio is treated as a behavior-driven product, not a collection of correctly configured screens; product QA is a first-class implementation task, not just registry/build validation.

nodes.label: College Analytics Model
nodes.rationale: Per-college aggregate view: active_students_7d, elo_distribution, branch_readiness, skill_map (strong/weak), company_track_readiness, and recruiter_ready_pool.

nodes.label: Execution Sandbox Model (Piston/Judge0)
nodes.rationale: Piston API primary with Judge0 CE fallback for coding challenges (10s/test, 30s total, 256MB cap, no filesystem writes/network); separate execution models for SQL (isolated Postgres schema per challenge), Frontend/React (iframe sandbox + esm.sh CDN), and Notebook/Python (Pyodide).

nodes.label: Arena Permissions Model + RLS
nodes.rationale: Row-Level Security enforces challenge_attempts writable only by owner, proof_artifacts readable by recruiters only when is_recruiter_visible=true, and leaderboard_snapshots publicly readable as proof of rank.

nodes.label: Proof Model (proof_artifacts)
nodes.rationale: Every submission creates a proof_artifacts record with trust_level (verified/ai_graded/self_reported) and a public_proof_url recruiters can check at /recruiter/candidates/:uid/proof.

nodes.label: Streak Computation Model (computeStreak)
nodes.rationale: Active day = >=1 submission (IST); freezes (limited per month) preserve the streak across a missed day; milestones from Ignition (3d) to Century Club (100d).

nodes.label: ProofDoc Model (§16)
nodes.rationale: Every scored submission mints one portable, recruiter-renderable ProofDoc: artifact-first (thumbnail is the dashboard/diagram/report, not a number), honest metadata (hints/attempt-number/validation-count disclosed), and replayable (dataset_seed + frozen inputs allow deterministic re-execution for anti-cheat/recruiter confidence).

nodes.label: Leaderboard Snapshot Strategy
nodes.rationale: Leaderboards are deliberately NOT computed per-request: a node-cron job snapshots into leaderboard_snapshots every 30 minutes so ranks are served with O(1) lookup instead of live aggregation.

nodes.label: Analytics / Telemetry (§11)
nodes.rationale: Ops-only metrics (completion time, pass rate, most-failed validator, hint usage, abandonment rate, AI feedback frequency, Challenge Payload Validator rejection rate) written to challenge_analytics_events to catch miscalibrated content and pipeline regressions early.

nodes.label: Dataset Versioning (§12)
nodes.rationale: Worked 'Amazon' dataset lineage (v1->v2 adds dedup-testing data quality issue, v3 adds a new returns table): dataset bug fixes ship as a new version rather than mutating in place, since mutating a dataset a student is actively querying would silently invalidate their in-flight ground_truth_compare/kpi_compare expectations.

nodes.label: Industry Catalog & Applicability (§8)
nodes.rationale: 8 industries mapped to strong/loose applicability per role family; Embedded/IoT, Android/iOS, and most QA roles are treated as industry-light since their Domain Challenges vary mainly by narrative flavor, not deep industry business logic.

nodes.label: Portfolio Artifact Types (§9)
nodes.rationale: code/report/dashboard/design/diagram, each carrying Portfolio Decision provenance (auto-published at score X vs. manually published below threshold) as the recruiter-facing honesty mechanism.

nodes.label: Recruiter Skill Evidence
nodes.rationale: Structured metadata on every portfolio artifact (skill, status, score, verification, difficulty, industry, scenario, skills demonstrated); Verification=Self-Selected keeps the below-threshold publish path honest rather than presenting it as equivalent to a verified pass.

nodes.label: Scenario Packs
nodes.rationale: Industry- and role-family-tagged bundles (Amazon, PayFast, MedCore, CloudNine) chaining scenario -> challenge templates, so a Data Analyst never gets handed a role-family-mismatched pack like PayFast: Auth Hardening.

nodes.label: Content Versioning Model (§10)
nodes.rationale: Rule of thumb across every content layer (Challenge Template, Workstation, Validator, Skill Graph, Scenario Pack, Dataset): version bumps affect only new starts; every in-progress student is pinned to the version snapshot recorded on their challengeInstanceId at creation, keeping grading deterministic as content evolves underneath it.

nodes.label: Assignment Engine (Mission Queue)
nodes.rationale: One ordered Mission Queue per user fed by four generators (Daily Mission, Adaptive Repair, Recruiter Challenges, Self-queued), ordered recruiter(deadline asc) -> daily -> repair -> self-queued; the homepage renders the queue, not a library.

nodes.label: Challenge Lifecycle State Machine
nodes.rationale: ASSIGNED -> OPENED -> IN_PROGRESS (autosave) <-> VALIDATED(n) -> SUBMITTED (frozen) -> SCORED -> PROOFED; one single state machine runs identically for every domain and every workstation.

nodes.label: Four-Layer Architecture (L1-L4)
nodes.rationale: L1 Arena Core (assignment engine, ELO economy, execution engines) -> L2 Universal Challenge Shell -> L3 sixteen lazy-loaded Workstation Renderers -> L4 Proof Pipeline; a new domain is added by writing one L3 module, L1/L2/L4 never fork.

nodes.label: Arena OS Redesign Vision (Challenge Operating System)
nodes.rationale: Reframes Arena from 'a place with challenges' (18 labels on one generic code-editor environment, library-first homepage) into one shell + one assignment engine + one proof pipeline + eighteen real work environments; inverts the 'label-over-environment' root disease behind system-design-in-a-markdown-box and dashboards that only appear after submission.
nodes.norm_label: arena os redesign vision (challenge operating system)

nodes.label: Contract A: Environment Fidelity
nodes.rationale: A challenge may only ship if its workstation contains the tools the real role actually uses; if the right workstation doesn't exist yet, the challenge waits — this is the quality gate that permanently kills 'generic editor with a different label'.

nodes.label: Contract B: Live Truth
nodes.rationale: Run/Validate/Preview all operate on the live workspace with real execution (WASM SQL/Python, sandboxed iframes, deterministic simulators) before submission; the user must never submit blind just to see their own output.

nodes.label: Contract C: Frozen Proof
nodes.rationale: Submit is the only destructive-ish action: it freezes the attempt into an immutable submission, scores it, and mints a recruiter-visible ProofDoc; the Submissions tab is an archive of frozen attempts, never the birthplace of output.

nodes.label: GitHub Clone and Cross-Repo Merge

nodes.label: Monorepo Multi-Subfolder Merge

nodes.label: Native CLAUDE.md Integration
nodes.rationale: graphify claude install writes a ## graphify section into the project's CLAUDE.md so future sessions check/rebuild the graph automatically without a manual /graphify invocation.

nodes.label: Post-Commit Auto-Rebuild Hook
nodes.rationale: Triggers once per git commit, re-runs AST extraction on files changed via git diff HEAD~1 and rebuilds graph.json/GRAPH_REPORT.md; doc/image changes are ignored and need a manual --update.

nodes.label: BFS/DFS Traversal Modes
nodes.rationale: BFS (default) for broad nearest-neighbor context; DFS (--dfs) for tracing a specific chain/dependency path, depth-limited to 6.

nodes.label: /graphify path and /graphify explain
nodes.rationale: path finds shortest route between two named concepts; explain gives a plain-language summary of one node's connections, both backed by the same graph.json.

nodes.label: --cluster-only Mode
nodes.rationale: Self-contained re-cluster of the existing graph; must not re-run Steps 5-9 since a prior build's cleanup already deleted the intermediate files they depend on (#1392).

nodes.label: --update Incremental Re-extraction
nodes.rationale: Only re-extracts new/changed files (detected via detect_incremental) to save tokens and time versus a full rebuild.

nodes.label: Fast-Path Query Check
nodes.rationale: If graphify-out/graph.json already exists and the request is a natural-language question, skip Steps 1-5 entirely and go straight to query — the graph is already built.

nodes.label: graphify Skill
nodes.rationale: Turns any folder of code/docs/papers/images/video into a queryable knowledge graph with community detection, an honest EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS audit trail, and three outputs (HTML, GraphRAG JSON, GRAPH_REPORT.md).

nodes.label: EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS Confidence Rubric
nodes.rationale: Discrete rubric (0.95/0.85/0.75/0.65/0.55) chosen because a continuous 0-1 range collapses to a bimodal distribution in production (>50% at 0.5, >40% at 0.85+); models follow discrete rubrics better than ranges.

nodes.label: Node ID Format Rule
nodes.rationale: Full repo-relative path (every segment) + normalized entity name, must match the AST extractor's ID scheme exactly, or re-extraction creates orphan ghost-duplicate nodes.

nodes.label: Constrained Query Vocabulary Expansion
nodes.rationale: graphify's matcher is case-folded substring + IDF with no stemming/synonyms/cross-language match; a wording mismatch between the user's question and the graph's labels collapses the answer to noise unless the query is first expanded against the graph's own extracted vocabulary (never inventing tokens).

nodes.label: Work Memory Self-Improving Loop
nodes.rationale: save-result --outcome useful|dead_end|corrected feeds graphify reflect, which regenerates LESSONS.md (preferred sources, dead ends, corrections) so future sessions don't re-derive the same dead ends.

nodes.label: Whisper Domain-Hint Prompt Generation
nodes.rationale: The host agent composes the Whisper initial_prompt itself from the corpus's god-node labels (no separate API call needed) since it is already a language model; falls back to a generic punctuation prompt for video-only corpora.

nodes.label: build_merge Replace-on-Re-extract
nodes.rationale: (#1344) Every source_file present in new_chunks is dropped from the base graph before merge, so changed files never leave stale nodes behind; prune_sources is reserved only for genuinely deleted files, not changed ones (would otherwise wrongly delete re-extracted content per #1178).

nodes.label: Manifest Semantic-Hash Staleness Guard
nodes.rationale: (#2015/#1948) Only files that actually produced output this run are stamped in the manifest; dispatched-but-unstamped files (failed chunks) have their semantic_hash cleared so the next --update re-queues them instead of treating lost content as done.

nodes.label: Graphify Honesty Rules
nodes.rationale: Never invent an edge (use AMBIGUOUS if unsure); never skip the corpus check warning; always show token cost; never hide cohesion scores; never run HTML viz on >5000 nodes without warning.

nodes.label: scripts/companyBackfill.mjs
nodes.rationale: dry-run reviewed by a human before --commit; confirmed it only creates new rows, never modifies jobs/offers/employment_history

nodes.label: skill_graph_nodes catalog table
nodes.rationale: shared, versioned catalog backfilled from roleConfig.js/skillGroups.js/user_skills distinct tuples so no learner's existing mastery data is orphaned

nodes.label: Student Challenges Page
nodes.rationale: Design principle: Student Challenges = ELO currency for students. Domain Challenges = proof of professional depth for recruiters. They share one ELO score but are filtered separately.

nodes.label: Recruiter Experience Notes
nodes.rationale: Makes the recruiter experience feel like a verifiable, timestamped portfolio — not a self-reported resume.

nodes.label: Dataset Versioning
nodes.rationale: A dataset bug fix ships as a new datasetVersion (e.g. v3) rather than mutating an existing version in place, because mutating a dataset a student is actively querying against would silently invalidate their in-flight ground_truth_compare/kpi_compare validator expectations.

nodes.label: Challenge Payload Validator Gate (two-gate model)
nodes.rationale: Every rejection is logged as its own Analytics event distinguishable by which gate rejected it, so a miscalibrated schema and a miscalibrated Capability Registry entry are diagnosable separately rather than both showing up as one generic rejection-rate metric.

nodes.label: Analytics / Telemetry Metrics
nodes.rationale: Feeds an internal ops dashboard only; exists to catch miscalibrated content and pipeline regressions early, not to gamify anything for the student.

nodes.label: Recruiter Skill Evidence
nodes.rationale: The Verification field (Verified vs Self-Selected) keeps the self-selected below-threshold publish path honest for recruiters instead of presenting it as equivalent to a verified pass.

nodes.label: Arena Content (package tree)
nodes.rationale: Splitting Arena Engine (zero domain-specific terms) from Arena Content makes 'the same Arena Engine powers every Career Family' an enforceable constraint: if the Engine ever needs a code change to consume a new content package, that signals the boundary was violated.

nodes.label: Assessment Layer (§6)
nodes.rationale: AI qualitative review is supplement only — it can explain why and nudge a sub-score within the validator-set range but can never override a failing validator result into a passing score; this is now enforced structurally by the pipeline shape rather than by code review catching it after the fact.

nodes.label: Capability Registry module (§1.1)
nodes.rationale: Belongs in Content, not Engine, because the registry (which workstations a role may use) is role-specific authored data like Skill Graphs and Scenario Packs; the Engine only checks the payload against the registry entry, never hardcodes per-role logic, which is what makes adding new roles/Career Families additive rather than requiring engine code changes.

nodes.label: Career Family (root taxonomy)
nodes.rationale: Reserving the Career Family taxonomy now costs nothing and saves a future refactor: adding a second family later means adding a new arena-content/ package tree, not touching the 11 Arena Engine backend modules, since none of them are IT-specific in their logic, only in their content.

nodes.label: Phase 1-4 Roadmap
nodes.rationale: Phase 3 picks Frontend Developer as the one complete Domain Role to prove end-to-end, because it exercises the React workstation, live-render probe validator, Industry variation, a real Scenario Pack, and the full Skill Dependency graph in one role — proving the framework rather than just designing it, before Phase 4 replicates to the remaining 39 roles.

nodes.label: Versioning (§7)
nodes.rationale: A student mid-progress on a content version stays pinned to that exact version even if a newer one ships mid-session; new starts always resolve to latest. This lets content improve continuously without invalidating in-flight work or retroactively changing what a completed Portfolio artifact was validated against.

nodes.label: arena.e2e@capabilio.test E2E test user + seed content
nodes.norm_label: arena.e2e@capabilio.test e2e test user + seed content

nodes.label: referral_codes P0 signup fix
nodes.rationale: referral_codes had no unique constraint on user_id, so the on_auth_user_created_referral trigger's ON CONFLICT (user_id) clause was invalid SQL, silently breaking all new-user signups platform-wide (not just Arena V2 test users) until an additive UNIQUE(user_id) constraint was added.

nodes.label: RLS Security Posture
nodes.rationale: No table has an authenticated INSERT/UPDATE policy; every write goes through a backend route using the service-role key after validation, mirroring the fix applied in the 2026-07-16 certification audit rather than reopening that risk for Arena V2.

nodes.label: mentor_disputes payout-hold derivation
nodes.rationale: open/investigating disputes exclude a booking from any payout batch, derived at query time from mentor_disputes rather than a booking.status value

nodes.label: mentor_idempotency_keys persisted table
nodes.rationale: real persisted idempotency (UNIQUE(idempotency_key, endpoint, user_id)), a valid retry replays the stored response, conflicting body/endpoint is 409, not just a debounce

nodes.label: applyRewards idempotency guard is check-then-insert, not transactional
nodes.rationale: protects against retry double-reward but not a genuine concurrent double-call race; no UNIQUE(assessment_id) constraint exists today unlike av2_submissions' UNIQUE(instance_id, attempt_number)
